answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by bonding stake to a scarce kernel of attested work history, not cheap identities. New agents start on an island of zero standing: they must pay gas and wait epoch delays before their attestations count. Only after peers countersign real verification at the settlement wharf does stake unlock. Flooding fake agents then costs repeated bond + time-locked capital per identity, so attack spend grows linearly while honest miners reuse one established kernel.
